turns.assessment: The outage is a simultaneous hard optical failure affecting many unrelated services, while E1 (roadm.S16) is the sole dependency common to every affected working path. The multi-channel LOS pattern on several S16-facing directions and the unchanged monitoring away from the failure region localize the cause to S16; single-client, single-channel, amplifier, and OTN-switch faults cannot explain the footprint. A failed WSS input port at roadm.S16 best matches the abrupt, broad signal blocking.

proposals.rationale: roadm.S16 is the only element shared by all affected working paths. A hard WSS input-port failure blocks every channel using that port and accounts for the synchronous service, protection, and optical LOS indications.

The OSC and amplifier input LOS indications are compatible with a cut near S16, but a cut on this single span does not explain the concurrent loss on the separate S16-S07 direction or the full affected-service footprint.
A switch-fabric failure at S16 could interrupt many ODUs, but it would produce ODU-layer failures rather than the observed OMS, OSC, and OCH loss-of-signal pattern.
proposals.note: site named; its node equipment does not document the mode

clarify.assessment: The evidence does not isolate one S16 WSS input port. Simultaneous LOS indications involve both the S03 and S07 degrees, while the S22 degree is also a possible ingress for affected channels; no port-specific observation uniquely selects one of the three resolutions.

llm_alone.decision: commit not to one place (3 locations); reported as a set
